note: Specs that must run at ONE worker. Everything else may run concurrently. Two mechanisms put a spec here. FOCUS: it opens the preferences window or drives a context menu, and throng closes menus when its window loses focus, so a second headed app closes them underneath it. CPU: it drives long-running real shells (ping, findstr loops), which starve at high worker counts and time out - the same failure mode that keeps CI at one worker (ci.yml). Membership is the mechanism plus anything measured failing at 6 workers, not observed failures alone, because contention produces a different failure set every run. Guarded by packages/ui/tests/unit/tier-plan.test.ts. See docs/testing.md. TIMING: it asserts a wall-clock ceiling (SC-002's two seconds from daemon kill to notice), which contention breaks without anything having regressed - measured at 2039ms with six workers against a 2000ms budget, where 1200ms of it is the grace by design. SPEC 034 added terminal-find and terminal-scrollback-nav under CPU, and the evidence is worth keeping because it also says what NOT to do: the 034 baseline found 13 real-shell specs failing at six workers, but classifying by mechanism alone would have moved 41 of them and made the suite SLOWER (~45.4 min modelled against ~40.3) - 28 of the 41 run perfectly well at six workers. Right-sizing the harness budgets fixed 11 of the 13 instead; these two still failed at a 30s terminal-output budget because they make a shell do real work (a 200-iteration cmd loop, a ping -n 7), so they are here by the mechanism rather than by a third budget increase. The mechanism identifies CANDIDATES; measurement decides which candidates actually need the tier. PER-ENTRY MECHANISMS (034 FR-001/SC-004, T035): `serial` is now an OBJECT rather than a list, because FR-001 says in terms that a bare list of filenames does not satisfy it - a reader could learn what the three mechanisms are from this note and still not learn which one put theme-fonts.e2e.ts here. An object rather than a parallel array so the list and its reasons cannot drift apart. Derived by READING all 122 files: a mechanical classifier was tried first and rejected, because its patterns matched "detached daemon" and any comment mentioning a shell prompt and produced 57 FOCUS out of 122 before anyone looked - an attribution invented to fill the column is worse than an empty one, since it reads as a judgement somebody made. UNATTRIBUTED IS A REAL VALUE, not a to-do: 14 files sit in this tier with no mechanism anyone can name from their contents, and several say so themselves - quick-open-toolbar.e2e.ts records in its own header that the preferences window which made it serial was removed, and tab-name-limit.e2e.ts says it deliberately AVOIDS the preferences window. They are candidates for the parallel tier, and candidates only: this file's own rule is that mechanism identifies candidates and measurement decides, so none of them moves without a worker-count measurement. One classification worth keeping: only context-menu.tsx registers a window-blur listener (it backs both the right-click menu and the cog dropdown), which is why files driving the tab picker, Quick Open, Go To Line, a hover popover or a confirm dialog are NOT focus-sensitive despite looking like it - those surfaces close on their own registry or on Escape, not on blur.
